subject: NimblePay — data audit recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimblePay — data audit recap & next steps
Attachments: nimblepay-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-data-privacy-one-pager.pdf (PDF)

Alex — thanks for the great conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so your security and infra teams have a single reference.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Transaction logs and free-text payment notes today include customer PII (email, phone, occasional IDs) and sometimes merchant notes with cardholder names.
- Security needs: no raw PANs or PHI should be sent to external processors; auditability for admin accesses; proof points for SOC2/PCI scoping.
- Retention tension: fraud team wants 180-day visibility for investigations, security wants PII redacted ASAP.

Current stack you described:
- Primary app and DB: self-hosted Postgres on GCP (us-west1).
- Observability: Splunk (managed account), Datadog for metrics.
- Processing: internal microservices push event streams to a Kafka topic before reaching downstream processors.

Success criteria (what NimblePay would consider a win):
1) No customer-identifying PII in third-party logs or in the inference request bodies beyond 7 days (redaction/hashing applied at ingress).
2) Ability to retain non-PII telemetry and tokens for up to 180 days for fraud analytics.
3) Audit trail (who/when) for any admin recall of original data — retention of those audit logs for 12 months.
4) KMS/HSM integration and control over encryption keys.
5) Evidence pack for SOC2 and a DPA/Datasubprocessor agreement in place.

Redwood recommended approach (initial proposal):
- Prefix/field-level redaction at the ingress gateway: configurable rules (regex + allowlist) so PII never leaves your environment in plaintext.
- Option A: Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS — allows inference runtime to run in your VPC and prevents tokens/raw text from being persisted to our hosted traces.
- Automatic tokenization/hashed identifiers stored in our analytics plane (hash salt under your KMS) so fraud queries can join events without raw PII.
- Audit logging: immutable admin audit events exported to your Splunk project; by default Redwood can stream access logs (admin id, action, timestamp) to an HTTPS endpoint.

Open questions / constraints to confirm from your side:
- Can NimblePay accept last4 and BIN only for payment records? Any strict PCI workflows we should avoid?
- Does your legal team require a fixed retention cutoff (e.g., 90 vs 180 days) or a policy-based retention window per customer?
- Any internal policy that forbids sending hashed identifiers to our analytics plane (some customers restrict even hashes)?

Next steps we propose (attached the mutual action plan):
1) Jordan/Marissa will share a short config sample for an ingress redaction policy by EOD tomorrow.
2) Security questionnaire to be sent to security@nimblepay.com and returned within 5 business days.
3) Schedule a technical walkthrough of Redwood Private (demo + network diagram) next week — suggested slots Tue/Wed morning PT.
4) Legal: start DPA / datasubprocessor conversation. Ben will draft an initial scoping note.

If that aligns, I’ll update the mutual action plan (attached) with dates. Happy to tweak based on your security constraints.

Thanks again — looking forward to continuing this.

—
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nimblepay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, security@nimblepay.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimblePay — data audit recap & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the summary and for capturing the open questions. A few clarifications from my side:
- We never store full PANs in logs (PCI policy) — we store last4 + BIN; full PANs are in a hardened vault.
- We cannot send any PHI or customer-provided SSNs to third parties; any PII must be redacted or replaced prior to transmission.
- Our fraud team does want 180-day visibility for transactional metadata, but that metadata must not contain unredacted PII.
- Splunk is managed by our security org (security@nimblepay.com) — we would prefer access logs (admin access audit) be forwarded there.

Could you include a brief sample of a redaction rule that shows how you handle free-text fields (e.g., payment notes)? Also, please include how the hashed identifier lifecycle is managed (rotate salt/key, ability to delete).

Alex Chen
Head of Payments Product
NimblePay
alex.chen@nimblepay.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Subject: Re: NimblePay — data audit recap & next steps

Alex / security team — looping in Neha (security lead) and Priya (solutions engineer) from our side.

Quick answers & tangible next items: 
- Jordan & I will deliver a redaction config sample (ingress regex + allowlist and a free-text scrubber example) by EOD today. That will include a small example showing replacement with hashed_id (SHA256 + customer KMS salt).
- For key management: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (we have integrations for Cloud KMS / AWS KMS) and can rotate salts on a customer schedule; we’ll include deletion/rotation notes in the doc.
- We’ll also prepare an export template for admin-access audit events so those can be streamed directly to your Splunk project.

Please confirm what works for the security contact.

Thanks — Marissa
